conclusion.justification: The report concludes that while the evidence quality is low and better trials are needed, the available evidence leans mildly positive, suggesting honey may modestly help acute cough symptoms in children over age 1.
conclusion.label: leans_endorse

report:
The evidence does not support a confident "no" — in fact, most current evidence leans mildly positive, though quality is weak.

The most authoritative source, the Cochrane systematic review, concludes there is "no strong evidence for or against the use of honey" for acute cough in children, while noting honey may relieve cough symptoms somewhat sooner than no treatment, and performs similarly to (not clearly better than) diphenhydramine, though possibly better than placebo/no treatment on some measures ([Cochrane](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007094.pub5/full); [Cochrane summary](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD007094_honey-acute-cough-children)). A more recent 2023 systematic review reached a similar cautious conclusion: "low quality evidence that honey may be more effective than cough medication or placebo/no treatment," but called for better-quality trials before firm conclusions can be drawn ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10570220/)).

So the honest evidentiary picture is: honey shows a modest, statistically favorable signal in trials (reduced cough frequency/severity, improved sleep) compared to no treatment or placebo, but the certainty of evidence is rated low to very low due to small trials, heterogeneity, and risk of bias. It is not that honey definitively doesn't work — rather, the evidence is too weak to make strong claims either way, though it leans toward showing benefit rather than none.

One clear point of universal agreement: honey must never be given to infants under 12 months due to infant botulism risk, regardless of cough benefit debates ([Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/symptoms/cough/expert-answers/honey/faq-20058031)).

**Conclusion:** The claim "honey does not help" is not well supported; current low-quality evidence suggests honey may modestly help cough symptoms in children over age 1, but better trials are needed to confirm this.
